data.hypothesis: An explicit float32 FMA chain for the softened squared distance may express the per-interaction multiply-add work compactly and help instruction scheduling while retaining the existing source traversal and target-mass cancellation. This is only a performance hypothesis; prior arithmetic variants failed a largest-size correctness check, so this candidate requires full correctness validation before timing.
data.notes: Only the distance expression changes. Keep the existing self-pair skip, float32 softening, velocity-then-position update order, and unchanged mass copy. No global fast math is enabled. The new candidate has not been measured; the supplied baseline is valid, while prior T4 arithmetic candidates were incorrect at the largest size, so no timing conclusion is available.
transformations: Replace the squared-distance expression with an explicit nested fmaf chain, keeping all distance arithmetic and softening in float32.
Retain the existing one-thread-per-target mapping, source traversal, direct target-mass cancellation, self-pair handling, integration order, and exact mass copy.
